# Using CodeForces Polygon with World Finals Style

This repo provides styles to replace Polygon-generated problem statements with ICPC World Finals styling.

Disclaimer: This is not an official ICPC style, and is only a hack to mimic the style used in ICPC World Finals problem statements.

## Usage

1. Replace `olymp.sty`, `statements.ftl` with the corresponding file generated by Polygon in the contest page `Properties/Files` only. 
2. (Optional) To display the banner, place `banner/statements-banner.pdf` in the same place, and uncomment `% \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{statements-banner.pdf}` line in `olymp.sty`.

If you want per-problem preview correct, you need to replace every problem's `statements.ftl` and `olymp.sty`, and place the banner PDF under **Statement Resource Files**. 

## Key Configuration

### Font Encoding Settings

The following are critical font settings located at the top of `olymp.sty`:

```latex
\RequirePackage{times}
\RequirePackage[T1]{fontenc}
```
Changing the encoding may lead to a loss of `times` font and affect the overall appearance.

### Intentionally Blank Pages

The following command enables "This page is intentionally left blank" functionality:

```latex
\intentionallyblankpagestrue
```

To disable this feature, comment out the line.

### Banner Header Settings

The page header banner is controlled by the following code:

```latex
\renewcommand{\@oddhead}{%
\parbox{\textwidth}{
\begin{center}
% \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{statements-banner.pdf}
\end{center}
}
}
```

- **Disable/Enable Banner**: Comment or uncomment the `\includegraphics` line to toggle the banner display.
- **Custom Banner**: Modify `banner/statements-banner.tex` and recompile to generate a new PDF.

### Better Sample Display

You have to hard code the sample for interactive problems by replacing the following code in `problem.tex` in each problem:

#### Run Twice, Non-Interactive, Only One Example
```latex
\Example
\begin{exampletwice}
<#list problem.sampleTests as test>
\exmpfile{${test.inputFile}}{${test.outputFile}}%
</#list>
\end{exampletwice}
```

#### Run Twice, Interactive
```latex
...
\Example
\begin{exampletwice}
\begin{interactzigzagtwice}
\interactread{First Run
1 2 3}%
\interactwrite{First Output
3 2 1}%
\end{interactzigzagtwice}%
\begin{interactzigzagtwice}
\interactread{Second Run
3 2 1}%
\interactwrite{Second Output
1 2 3}%
\interactread{OK}%
\interactwrite{OK}%
\end{interactzigzagtwice}%
\end{exampletwice}
...
```

### Example with Explanation on First Sample

```
...
<#if  (problem.sampleTests?size>0)>
\Example<#if  (problem.sampleTests?size>1)>s</#if>

\begin{example}
<#assign insertedAfterFirstSample = false />
<#list problem.sampleTests as test>
\exmpfile{${test.inputFile}}{${test.outputFile}}%
<#if !insertedAfterFirstSample>
<#assign insertedAfterFirstSample = true />
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}
\normalfont\normalsize
 \catcode`\ =10
 \catcode`\^^M=5
 \let\par\endgraf
\textbf{Explanation of Sample 1:} Test case details...
\end{minipage}
</#if>
</#list>
\end{example}
</#if>
...
```
